text:
alerts-bot: sso-anomaly detected — 14 accounts, lots of very short-lived sessions (<30s) from dozens of rotating ASNs across us/eu regions. Success responses on token exchange. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/1788882222

nate: Oncall nate here. Which client/app is involved? any org-admins affected?

emily: quick look — token_exchange path for web SSO. Sampling shows user_agent blank and device_agent unset. Looks like an automated client or script.

ashwin: ran quick audit query: `SELECT user_id, count(*) as hits FROM auth_audit.sso_exchanges WHERE ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY hits DESC LIMIT 30;` several service accounts + 3 dev accounts at top.

olivia: FYI I rotated the CI runner client_secret ~7m ago to remediate a leak. Only targeted the `ci-runner` app.

nate: hm — if that was the rotation we'd expect failed exchanges for old clients, not successful short sessions. Alerts show token issuance succeeded.

emily: checking full traces... tokens are being minted (200), then immediately the session-monitor revokes them due to anomaly rule (session duration ~12-28s). So either replay followed by auto-revocation or a config toggling TTL.

infra-ops: we pushed a small RBAC/session patch to auth-service ~9m ago. There was a payload typo that set SSO session TTL to 30s for web clients. Rolling a rollback now.

ashwin: can someone query KMS audit for any unauthorized key usage in the same window? `gcloud kms operations list --filter="createTime>\"$(date -d '10 minutes ago' -Iseconds)\""` — we need to rule out key compromise.

olivia: KMS audit shows only one rotation call (my CI key) and a standard automated rotation for backup keys. No unexpected usage of production signing keys.

nate: good catch. infra-ops, how long to rollback?

infra-ops: rollback complete (at +380s). TTL reverted to normal. Keeping the old deployment cordoned while we run canary checks.

emily: containment items: 1) rolled back bad deploy, 2) temporarily disabled `ci-runner` client until we rotate and revalidate, 3) WAF rule added to block the high-churn ASN ranges seen in the logs.

ashwin: creating a ticket with the audit queries, sample redacted tokens and the list of impacted accounts: INC-2026-451. Assigning infra, idp, security.

olivia: I'll re-run CI-client rotation as a coordinated change with a checklist so it doesn't collide with session config changes.

nate: next steps: (a) postmortem + timeline, (b) add a deploy-time test to verify session TTLs after any auth-service rollout, (c) RBAC gating for client_secret rotations so they require a brief maintenance window and automated checks, (d) increase auth-audit retention to 90d for faster sleuthing.

infra-ops: logging followup: we've captured heap of traces and preserved logs in S3://sec-incidents/1788882222. Will attach to INC ticket.

emily: closing alert for now — monitoring for recurrence for 2 hours. If anything pops, @nate and @ashwin please escalate. :thumbsup:

nate: Thanks team — good catch on the rollback. We'll run the post-incident at 10:30PT tomorrow.
